Zhang, and Sanglu Lu. 2021. Thru-the-wall eavesdropping on loudspeakers
via RFID by capturing sub-mm level vibration. In Proceedings of the ACM on
Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies, Vol. 5. 1–25.
paper_level_summary_zh: 本论文在相关工作部分将目标论文列为RFID振动感知的现有工作之一，但未对其亚毫米级精度进行单独描述或评价。引用主要集中在普通相关工作列举，未提供具体技术细节或肯定性评价。

evidences.evidence_quote: some works use RF signals, such as Wi-Fi [48], mmWave [3,16,22,23,43,44,51,59], and RFID [7,30,46], to capture surrounding object vibration for sensing speaker-produced sound [3,22,23,30,44–46,48] or capture body motions for sensing human-speaking sound [7,16,43,51].
evidences.evidence_context: On the other hand, some works use RF signals, such as Wi-Fi [48], mmWave [3,16,22,23,43,44,51,59], and RFID [7,30,46], to capture surrounding object vibration for sensing speaker-produced sound [3,22,23,30,44–46,48] or capture body motions for sensing human-speaking sound [7,16,43,51].
